162	The question arises, which the Rishonim ask: what does it mean to say about
163	HaShem that He does not take a bribe? Where
164	does a bribe come into this matter of not taking a bribe?
165	The Ramban in this week's Parashah speaks in a few words, briefly,
166	not at length, in a few words, about this subject
167	of not taking a bribe. The Ramban writes: even a
168	complete chasid who commits a transgression, God forbid, one chasid,
169	chasid meaning a person of high virtue. It doesn't mean
170	a chasid in the sense of the Chasidic movement or
171	the Lithuanians. I am speaking to you about a chasid: this is
172	a person of great virtue. We all know that chasidut
173	is on the ladder of values of Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair, a very high
174	level. Even a complete chasid who commits
175	a transgression, HaShem will not take one of his mitzvot as a bribe
176	to atone for him. There is no such situation, writes the Ramban, that HaShem
177	removes one mitzvah and atones for him for
178	the transgression. There is no deducting, but He will punish him for his sins
179	and complete for him all his good deeds. HaShem does not
180	take mitzvot as a bribe and say: you committed a transgression,
181	please, come, I will deduct it. Rather, what? He says, very simply:
182	you will receive punishment for the transgression and you will receive reward for
183	the mitzvah. These are the words of the Ramban on what is said here, "He will not
184	take a bribe." The same words can also be found
185	in Rabbeinu Ovadia Sforno. He writes: "He will not remove at all
186	from the punishment of the transgression for the sake of the merit of a mitzvah that he did." One who sinned,
187	there is no such thing that He will remove any of the punishment of the transgression
188	for the sake of the merit of one mitzvah, for, as it is written
189	in the Gemara in Tractate Sotah, page 21,
190	a mitzvah does not extinguish a transgression. A mitzvah does not succeed in extinguishing a transgression. And all this
191	teaches that you should not trust, if you sin, to be saved by any merit
192	from the punishment at all. There is no situation where you say: listen,
193	I committed a transgression, let them deduct mitzvot for me. There is no such thing.
194	No mitzvot will be deducted for you, except through
195	complete teshuvah. Only if a person repents can the
196	transgression be removed. There is no situation of removing a
197	transgression in exchange for a mitzvah. These are the words of Rabbeinu Ovadia
198	Sforno, which come from the Ramban, with somewhat more detail.
